# Balcony Vegetable Garden

I have been thinking about this project for months now. Last winter I spent way too many evenings scrolling through gardening forums and watching YouTube videos about container growing. Our apartment balcony gets about six hours of direct sun in the summer, which should be enough for most vegetables if I am careful about placement. The railing is sturdy enough to hold a few larger pots, and I already have a small shelf unit I can use for herbs and seedlings.

The main focus this year is tomatoes, specifically the [[Sungold]] cherry variety. I started the seeds indoors on February 20th. They germinated quickly, within five days, and the seedlings are looking strong under the grow light I set up in the spare bedroom. The plan is to transplant them outside after the last frost, which around here usually means around May 10th. I am a little nervous about timing because last year we had a surprise cold snap in mid-May, but I can always bring the pots inside for a night or two if the forecast looks bad.

For the containers I decided on 5-gallon fabric pots. They are lightweight, breathable, and supposedly help prevent root circling. I ordered a pack of ten but will probably only use four or five for the tomatoes this season. The rest can hold peppers, basil, or maybe some lettuce. The fabric pots dry out faster than plastic, so I will need to stay on top of watering, especially during July and August when it gets really hot on the balcony.

Soil mix has taken up most of my note-taking time lately. After reading a dozen different recipes I settled on a blend that should be light enough for containers yet rich in nutrients. For every 5-gallon pot I am using:

- 40% high-quality potting mix (the kind with perlite already in it)
- 30% compost from the community garden pile
- 20% coco coir to help with water retention
- 10% worm castings for extra nutrients

I also mixed in a handful of slow-release organic fertilizer pellets and a tablespoon of mycorrhizal fungi powder per pot. The first test batch I made last weekend felt really nice in my hands, loose and spongy without being too heavy. I let it sit in the pots for a week to settle before I transplant the Sungold seedlings.

Fertilizing schedule is every two weeks with diluted fish emulsion. I picked up a bottle of the liquid kind that smells terrible but the plants seem to love it. I will start feeding about two weeks after transplant and continue through the end of August. The plan is to alternate between the fish emulsion and a compost tea I want to try making from the balcony worm bin I set up last month.

I still need to figure out support for the tomato plants. Sungold is indeterminate so it will get tall. Maybe some bamboo stakes or a simple trellis attached to the balcony railing. I should add a note to pick up some soft ties and maybe some mulch to keep the soil cooler.

Other things I want to grow this year include:
- Sweet basil in the smaller pots
- A couple of jalapeño plants
- Marigolds for pest control and because they look cheerful
- Maybe some bush beans if I have space left

The whole project feels a bit ambitious for a first serious attempt at balcony gardening, but I am excited. There is something really satisfying about stepping outside with a cup of coffee and picking fresh tomatoes for lunch. I will update this note as things progress, especially once the plants are outside and I can start tracking actual growth and any problems that come up.
